evidence: store.py:265 calls collection.get(include=..., limit=page_size, offset=offset) with a correct pagination loop (266-272). agent_memory.py:144-159 _get_collection returns a real chromadb client collection (client.get_collection/create_collection), not a custom wrapper. The chromadb package source (Collection.get signature) is not in the head view, so limit/offset support could not be confirmed by reading. Not run: inspecting the installed chromadb Collection.get signature.

store.py:259-272 iter_records pages with collection.get(limit=256, offset=offset) and advances offset by len(ids), with no explicit ordering, so it does rely on stable order. Whether Chroma guarantees stable order, and what concurrent writes do to offsets, is a property of the chromadb library, which is not in the supplied views. I did not run or read chromadb, so the guarantee is unsettled. No repository requirement was shown broken.

store.py:275-293 _records_from_result uses `or []` only on ids/metadatas (Chroma returns plain lists there), and handles embeddings (possibly numpy) with `is not None` and len(), never truthiness (278, 286). Index access is bounds-guarded (282, 286), so misaligned/short lists degrade safely. _coerce_embedding (230-246) iterates raw into floats, handling numpy rows. Each page is self-contained (index-local, no cross-page state), and iter_records (259-272) applies it per page with offset advancing by len(ids).

store.py:229-230 _coerce_embedding is @staticmethod(raw); :274-275 _records_from_result is @staticmethod and calls MemoryStore._coerce_embedding at :287; get_one calls self._coerce_embedding at :313, valid for a staticmethod.

admin.py:165-180: matching_records is a single generator that increments total per match. heapq.nlargest(limit, it, key=...) consumes the iterable once, so total counts all matches. CPython documents nlargest(n, it, key) as equivalent to sorted(it, key=key, reverse=True)[:n], and its implementation uses a decreasing order counter, so ties keep input order (earlier first). The test at tests/unit/test_memory_bounds.py:121-134 expects ids 0..999 for equal timestamps and total 1200, which matches. The limit=0 branch drains the generator so total is still complete. Order is deterministic given a deterministic store iteration order.

Only in-repo caller of memory_admin.list_memories in src is server.py:539, passing limit from a tool param typed Annotated[int, Field(ge=0, le=1000)] default 1000 (server.py:526), so never None or >1000. UI widget calls the tool with LIST_LIMIT=1000 (memory_admin.html:362,708). cli.py has no references. admin.py:161-162 enforces int in 0..1000 else MemoryInputError. Other callers are tests only.

src/sqllens/_errors.py:16 defines validation_error_lines(exc, *, with_type: bool) -> list[str]; it builds lines only from err loc, msg and (optionally) type, never the 'input' field (lines 19-25). admin.py:248 calls it with with_type=False, matching the keyword.

schema.py:17 defines QUESTION_MAX = 1000 at module level; schema.py:60 SqlPair.question uses Field(max_length=QUESTION_MAX); admin.py:39 imports it and admin.py:265 uses len(question) > QUESTION_MAX to decide whether the echoed question is returned.

admin.py:246-252 maps ValidationError and TypeError to bounded messages. In schema.py:55-94 SqlPair/SchemaDoc are plain pydantic models; the only validators raise ValueError (via _require_non_blank), which pydantic wraps in ValidationError. Wrong-typed or oversized field values and extra keys (extra=forbid) give ValidationError. A non-mapping raw (str, list, None, int) makes `Model(**raw)` raise TypeError at call time (argument after ** must be a mapping). Non-string dict keys also give TypeError. BaseModel.__init__ takes self positionally-only, so a 'self' key does not break this. No malformed shape reaches the generic log-and-fallback branch.

admin.py:241-243 raises MemoryInputError (a ValueError subclass, admin.py:62) with a fixed bounded message (name and cap only). The only caller of memory_admin.add_memories in src is server.py:647; it catches MemoryInputError at 650 and re-raises RuntimeError(str(exc)), which the MCP tool layer reports as an isError result. A grep of src found no CLI or UI callers. Any other exception is caught at 652 and replaced with a generic message.

server.py:526 uses Annotated[int, Field(ge=0, le=1000)] with Field/Annotated imported (lines 22, 26). FastMCP's func_metadata builds a pydantic arguments model from the annotated params, so the JSON schema gets minimum/maximum and call arguments are validated before fn runs (handler body starts at 537). The test tests/integration/test_memory_bounds.py:34-44 checks the published maximum, an isError result for 1001, and reader not called. I did not run the test or read the installed mcp source; this rests on known FastMCP behavior.

agent_memory.py:48-50 keeps Optional[int] with default 10 and ge=1, le=100; in pydantic v2 constraints apply only to non-None int values, so explicit None validates. agent_memory.py:168 uses args.limit or 10, handling None. registry.py:210-213 wraps args_model.model_validate in try/except Exception and returns ToolResult (line 213), so out-of-range limits become a tool-level failure, not an unhandled exception.

io.py:135 and :170 call _enforce_item_caps (io.py:68-86, uses MAX_BUNDLE_ITEMS) after parse in parse_json/parse_csv. admin.py:241-243 add_memories checks len(items) > MAX_BUNDLE_ITEMS as the first statement, before item validation (256+) and before any store access; store is not touched in the loop. Hostile input: oversized sql_pairs list to add_memories raises MemoryInputError before SqlPair(**raw) or store use.

admin.py:161-189: limit validated 0..MAX; total increments for every record passing the memory_type filter inside matching_records(); limit==0 branch (178-180) drains the generator so total counts the full filtered scan; limit>0 uses heapq.nlargest(limit,...) retaining at most limit candidates. store.py:263-272 iter_records uses page_size=256 with collection.get(limit,offset). Tested input: limit=0 with a type filter, total is still fully counted. Rows with non-dict metadata are skipped (store.py:283), but they cannot be classified to any memory_type so are not 'matching'.

Exception details are scrubbed: validation_error_lines (_errors.py:16-25) emits only loc/msg, admin.py:246-252 maps TypeError/other to fixed strings, importer.py:107-114 uses fixed message 'Failed to save memory item; check the server logs.'. But admin.py:264-269 echoes the caller's raw `question` (<=1000 chars, any string) in the error entry of a pair that failed validation (e.g. bad sql), and admin.py:293,300 echoes the question for storage failures. So raw caller-supplied input from a rejected item is returned, contradicting the CHANGELOG's absolute wording (CHANGELOG.md:84-85). Impact is minor: it is the caller's own value, length-capped, used for identification.

importer.py:107-115 appends ImportItemError(kind, index, fixed message) and logs the exception with kind/index. Consumers of .message (server.py:465, cli.py:502, schema.py:134, admin.py:300) only format or pass the text through, and none parses it. The only tests asserting on the message (tests/unit/test_memory_import_export.py:223,244) already expect the fixed text. Entries stay distinguishable by the kind and index fields, which are retained (admin.py:290-300 remaps by index). Only the message text is identical across items.

store.py:265 calls collection.get(include=include, limit=page_size, offset=offset) with keywords only, page_size=256; PagedCollection.get (test_memory_bounds.py:79) is keyword-only (include, limit=None, offset=0), asserts 0<limit<=256, and returns a dict with ids/metadatas/embeddings (None when 'embeddings' not in include, line 89). _records_from_result (store.py:276-278) uses got.get and treats embeddings None as absent, consistent with chromadb's Collection.get(ids, where, limit, offset, where_document, include) returning embeddings None when not included. Chroma signature not read from source; based on known API.

conftest.py:93-126 make_server yields _build, whose __globals__ are conftest's module globals; build_asgi_app is imported there (line 36) and looked up globally at line 108, so setitem takes effect. _build accepts auth: AuthConfig (line 102). server.py:481 imports `memory_admin` from sqllens.memory and calls memory_admin.list_memories (539) via attribute lookup, so patching admin.list_memories intercepts it. admin.add_memories calls import_bundle through module global (admin.py:36, 286), so patching admin.import_bundle intercepts it; the item-cap check (admin.py:243) raises before it.

export_memories JSON (admin.py:357-366) emits {sql_pairs:[{question,sql}], schema_docs:[{content}]}, the add_memories argument shape. add_memories rejects only when a block exceeds MAX_BUNDLE_ITEMS=10_000 (admin.py:241-243; schema.py:41), so stores at or under the cap re-ingest directly. test_memory_admin_tools.py:367-392 feeds an export back unmodified and gets saved_count==3 with no errors. The CLI import path applies the same cap (io.py:79-86 _enforce_item_caps). Docs say to split larger exports into batches (admin.py:20,314-315; docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md:389; docs/internal/agent/memory.md:184,268; docs/external/managing-memory.md:65-66), and I found no other documented remediation. Limit: the round-trip test uses 3 items, not a store at the cap. The cap logic is straightforward and shows the property holds at 10,000.
